nodes.name: Classical Philology
nodes.description: The study of Greek and Latin language and texts through critical editing and interpretation.

nodes.name: Ancient Greek Literature
nodes.description: The literary corpus of ancient Greece from Homer to late antiquity.

nodes.name: Latin Literature
nodes.description: The literary corpus of Rome from the Republic to late antiquity.

nodes.name: Ancient Greek Language
nodes.description: The study of the Ancient Greek language in its dialects and history.

nodes.name: Latin Language
nodes.description: The study of the Latin language from archaic to medieval usage.

nodes.name: Classical Mythology
nodes.description: The myths, gods, and heroic narratives of Greece and Rome.

nodes.name: Epigraphy
nodes.description: The study of inscriptions on stone, metal, and other durable materials.

nodes.name: Papyrology
nodes.description: The study of texts preserved on papyrus and other ancient writing materials.

nodes.name: Numismatics
nodes.description: The study of ancient coins and their historical evidence.

nodes.name: Classical Reception Studies
nodes.description: The study of how Greco-Roman antiquity has been received and reinterpreted.

nodes.name: Byzantine Studies
nodes.description: The study of the Byzantine Empire's language, literature, and culture.

nodes.name: Textual Criticism
nodes.description: The method of reconstructing ancient texts from surviving manuscripts.

nodes.name: Classical Paleography
nodes.description: The study of ancient handwriting and the dating of manuscripts.

nodes.name: Greek Epic
nodes.description: The epic poetry of ancient Greece, especially the Homeric poems.

nodes.name: Greek Tragedy
nodes.description: The tragic drama of Athens, including Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides.

nodes.name: Greek Comedy
nodes.description: The comic drama of Athens, from Aristophanes to Menander.

nodes.name: Greek Lyric
nodes.description: The lyric poetry of archaic and classical Greece.

nodes.name: Greek Historiography
nodes.description: The historical writing of ancient Greece, from Herodotus to Polybius.

nodes.name: Latin Epic
nodes.description: The epic poetry of Rome, especially Virgil's Aeneid.

nodes.name: Latin Lyric
nodes.description: The lyric poetry of Rome, including Horace and Catullus.

nodes.name: Latin Comedy
nodes.description: The comic drama of Rome, including Plautus and Terence.

nodes.name: Latin Historiography
nodes.description: The historical writing of Rome, including Livy and Tacitus.

nodes.name: Latin Rhetoric
nodes.description: The art of oratory and persuasion in Roman culture.

nodes.name: Greek Epigraphy
nodes.description: The study of inscriptions in the Greek language.

nodes.name: Latin Epigraphy
nodes.description: The study of inscriptions in the Latin language.
